events.continuity_hook: Follows the Madison booking once the selected Milwaukee routing becomes less comfortable before the early clinic day.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the revised arrival plans, confirm late rental-car pickup and hotel check-in, and decide whether the original Milwaukee strategy still protects Monday morning readiness.
events.scenario_brief: A carrier retime pushes Kara's Sunday Tampa-to-Milwaukee arrival later than expected, leaving a narrower window to collect the rental car and drive to Madison before a Monday 7:15 a.m. clinic start. The Wednesday afternoon return is unchanged, but the late pickup raises a practical choice between keeping the terminal rental, switching to an airport hotel near Milwaukee for the first night, or paying more to connect into Madison. The downtown suite hotel still confirms the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, and fitness room.

events.continuity_hook: Closes out the Madison logistics after the routing and lodging are set, with only local arrival details left to tighten.
events.interaction_goal: Lock the Monday arrival buffer, verify parking details, and set the simple food-and-room plan for the first morning.
events.scenario_brief: Four days before departure, the Madison clinic sends final access notes: the main lobby will be closed early Monday, demo gear must come through a loading-side therapy entrance, and visitor parking requires a plate number. Kara's flights, Wednesday afternoon return, and downtown suite stay remain in place. The remaining items are how to handle the late Sunday drive, whether to make a grocery stop or rely on delivery, and how early to leave the hotel Monday morning.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a personal recovery episode after several work-heavy trips make a partner weekend the next travel priority.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Asheville versus Greenville-Spartanburg access, narrow lodging areas by drive time and recovery setup, and identify cancellation and parking details to verify before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After the Madison visit and a heavy spring teaching stretch, Kara and her partner start planning a late-June Thursday-to-Monday active recovery weekend in the Blue Ridge area. She can leave Tampa only after a Thursday morning course wrap-up, and her partner wants one longer hike, one lighter waterfall day, and enough downtime for recovery. Airfare into Asheville is high, Greenville-Spartanburg has better timing with a rental car, and lodging options split between a downtown hotel with strong ratings but limited recovery facilities and a mountain lodge farther out that lists a queen room, in-room coffee, mini-fridge, pool, hot tub, and fitness room.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the partner weekend once the viable airport routing and lodging trade-off are clear enough to book.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the airport routing, book the lodging and rental car, and handle seat selection around sitting together if they take the flights.
events.scenario_brief: The Asheville-area plan narrows after the Thursday evening Greenville-Spartanburg flight and Monday afternoon return price out better than flying into Asheville, and a compact rental car is available without a prepaid penalty. The mountain lodge keeps the best recovery setup but requires a longer drive after landing; the downtown hotel is easier for restaurants and evening logistics but has no hot tub and only a small fitness room. The main decision is whether the quieter lodge is worth the drive and higher rate for a trip built around hiking recovery rather than city time.

events.continuity_hook: Revisits the partner weekend after lodging and trail information change part of the reason Kara and her partner chose the lodge.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to keep the lodge or switch properties, adjust the hiking plan, and confirm any cancellation timing before the deadline.
events.scenario_brief: Two weeks before the Blue Ridge weekend, the lodge alerts guests that the hot tub will be closed the first night for resurfacing, while the pool and fitness room remain open. A nearby resort has an outdoor hot tub available and a strong rating but only king rooms left at a steeper rate, and a cabin option has a kitchenette but no fitness access. The hiking plan is also affected by a trail closure on the route they had ranked first.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next late-summer teaching episode after the personal weekend planning settles and a hospital host begins locking lab dates.
events.interaction_goal: Build a practical flight-and-hotel shortlist, compare commute convenience against room reliability, and list what the hospital must confirm about setup access, gear storage, and Saturday finish time.
events.scenario_brief: In early July, a children's hospital in Columbus asks Kara to teach a Friday-Saturday pediatric neuro-motor lab in late August, with a Thursday evening room walk-through requested and a Saturday teardown that could finish at 3:30 p.m. or slip closer to 5:00. She can leave Tampa after a Thursday midday faculty call, and flight choices split between a late-afternoon nonstop and a lower-fare connection arriving close to 11:00 p.m. The hospital-adjacent hotel has the shortest commute but uneven recent reviews and unclear mini-fridge availability, while a better-rated suite hotel 15 minutes away confirms a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room but no hot tub.
